review.summary: The human CSB–PGBD3 fusion binds selected MER85 sequences.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 Methods and Figure4 compare partially purified insect-expressed human fusion protein and standalone PGBD3 in EMSA with six MER85 elements and nonspecific competitor. Four elements bind strongly in the tested assay. This supports sequence-selective DNA binding by the fusion, not canonical CSB equivalence or nuclease/transposase activity. The reported unpublished ChIP-seq is not used as an independently verified experiment.

source.goName: positive regulation of defense response to virus by host

review.summary: The fusion induces an antiviral-like transcriptional program, but effective host defense remains unresolved.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 Results3.3–3.6 show an unusual interferon-like expression program in human CSB-null UVSS1KO cells, including antiviral effectors and STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation without induced interferons or canonical Tyr701 activation. These are positive regulatory observations. The bridge to GO:0002230 functional host defense, including limiting viral replication, is not resolved by the inspected assays. This is not a universal virus-challenge requirement or a claim that the response is false; retain uncertainty about this particular process endpoint.

review.summary: The fusion positively regulates STAT1 expression in the tested human-cell context.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 Results3.3–3.4 and expression/protein measurements show elevated STAT1 after expression of human CSB–PGBD3 in CSB-null UVSS1KO cells. Retain this contextual expression-regulatory assertion as non-core. Preserve the imported STAT1 extension and distinguish the fusion from full-length CSB, which can suppress the fusion-induced program.

review.summary: The fusion positively regulates the measured innate-response gene set.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 Results3.3–3.6 use expression profiling and follow-up measurements to show induction of interferon-associated genes by human CSB–PGBD3 in UVSS1KO cells. Retain this supported contextual gene-expression regulation and the exact imported high-throughput source/extension. It does not by itself establish an antiviral phenotype or direct binding to each gene promoter.

source.goName: positive regulation of peptidyl-serine phosphorylation of STAT protein

review.summary: The fusion promotes STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation under the tested conditions.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 Results3.4/Figure3 distinguish increased STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation from absent canonical Tyr701 phosphorylation in the fusion-expressing human cells. Retain positive regulation of STAT serine phosphorylation as non-core; do not describe the fusion as the kinase or as a direct phosphotransfer enzyme.

review.summary: The fusion contributes positively to repair readouts, with full-length CSB distinguished.
review.reason: PMID:22483866 separates human full-length CSB and CSB–PGBD3 constructs in UVSS1KO cells and measures UV RNA recovery/host-cell reactivation. Fusion-alone and coexpression effects support a contextual positive repair-regulatory contribution. Preserve this external product and the exact IMP/IGI source context, including the full-length CSB interaction partner for the IGI record; do not assign the canonical CSB ATPase mechanism to the fusion.

review.summary: Nuclear localization is independently demonstrated for tagged human CSB–PGBD3.
review.reason: The P0DP91 SL-0191 mapping is supported by PMID:26218421 Results/Figure 3 and Methods Laser micro-irradiation and imaging: human U2OS cells express the explicitly constructed CSB–PGBD3-RFP fusion, with nuclear signal and recruitment to nuclear damage. Chromatin-associated fusion-eGFP is examined separately in HeLa cells. The construct caption identifies the fusion coding sequence and tags. Rhesus oocyte immunohistochemistry is a separate species/antibody experiment, and human ovary western blots establish expression rather than cellular localization. This decision belongs to the external fusion record and is not appended to the 139 canonical source contexts.

source_entities.comment: The external-product nuclear location is corroborated with an explicitly tagged human fusion construct.

review.summary: Tagged human CSB–PGBD3 localizes in the nucleus.
review.reason: PMID:26218421 Methods and Figure3 use the full human fusion construct tagged with RFP in U2OS cells and GFP in HeLa cells, demonstrating nuclear laser-damage recruitment and peroxide-associated chromatin localization. This independently supports nucleus for the fusion. Rhesus-oocyte localization is a separate experiment and is not represented as endogenous human oocyte imaging; no defined nuclear-body class is inferred.

review.summary: The precise nucleoplasm assignment is not uniquely resolved for the fusion.
review.reason: HPA071297 reports this location, and its 141-residue antigen exactly matches P0DP91 residues 472–612. However the same sequence occurs in standalone PGBD3 Q8N328 residues 4–144; the western annotation reports a predicted 119.5 kDa band plus additional bands. The image therefore does not uniquely distinguish the fusion from standalone PGBD3. PMID:26218421 independently establishes nuclear localization and damage-associated chromatin recruitment of tagged human fusion protein, but the inspected Methods/Results do not identify the more precise nucleoplasm compartment as a distinct product-specific finding. Preserve this external assertion separately and do not infer absence of the location.
